key_catalyst: Brent crude jumping over 6% on a Houthi tanker attack and US-Saudi strikes in Iraq — a fresh, materialized escalation of the Middle East oil-supply shock.
reasoning: The morning HOLD rested on a de-escalating premise — falling oil removing the macro-shock pillar and chip weakness being merely anticipatory — but the intraday session inverted both pillars: Brent surged over 6% on a fresh Houthi tanker attack plus new US-Saudi strikes in Iraq (a materialized, broadening geopolitical shock, not an anticipatory jitter), while chips deteriorated further (Micron on CXMT/DRAM pressure, SNDK dragging the Nasdaq). QQQ fell -1.62%, but the dominant catalyst is a hard supply shock that is ESCALATING into the close, not resolving. What remains unresolved is where oil settles in the Asia/Europe overnight window — precisely where this premium re-prices — with a Fed decision compounding uncertainty.
